name: Citizenship by Descent and by Marriage

requirements.blocker_text: This requires a Turkish mother or father (in or out of wedlock, with paternity established for out-of-wedlock cases). Citizenship is attributed automatically at birth. A child born stateless in Turkey also acquires citizenship. Jus soli alone (mere birth in Turkey) does NOT confer citizenship.

This requires being married to a Turkish citizen for at least 3 years, with the marriage continuing and a genuine family union — not automatic on marriage itself, and the applicant must not pose a security/public-order risk. Provincial citizenship examination commissions assess authenticity through interviews and shared documentation. No fixed statutory language test is codified for this route.
requirements.fix_path: Maintain the marriage for the required period and prepare for the authenticity assessment.

evidence_required.document: Birth certificate and evidence of the parent's Turkish citizenship (descent group)
Marriage certificate and evidence of a genuine, ongoing family union (marriage group)

sources.title: Directorate General of Population and Citizenship Affairs — Turkish Citizenship Law No. 5901, Arts. 7-8, 16

notes: descent group: selection_method genuinely 'automatic' at birth, structurally identical to France's droit du sang and Japan's descent rule — no application needed for the initial attribution itself. marriage group: EXPLICITLY NOT automatic on marriage — a genuinely important distinction some secondary sources blur, since Turkey requires 3 years of continued, genuine union before eligibility, assessed by provincial commissions specifically screening for marriage-of-convenience fraud. No fixed statutory language test exists for the marriage-based route — a real and confirmed absence, distinct from most other countries' marriage-based citizenship routes in this dataset (UK, Germany, Portugal, Spain, France all specify a CEFR level for spousal naturalisation). Dual citizenship confirmed permitted for both groups, consistent with Turkey's broader dual-citizenship-friendly posture across every route in this dataset.
